When Apple unveiled the Apple Watch Series 12, two features stood out the most: the all-new Siri Recap feature, and a significantly upgraded heart rate monitor. While these two features were part of my reason for buying the new Apple Watch, I found there was even more to惊喜.

Battery and Charging

Although Apple's website does not list any additional battery life improvement for the Apple Watch Series 12 over the Series 11, the battery does indeed feel more durable. As I wrote before, before using the Apple Watch Series 12, I had been a WHOOP user; although I always wore my Apple Watch, I never used it to track sleep.

After the keynote ended, I decided to give Apple Watch's sleep tracking a try. However, on my Series 11, balancing sleep tracking and charging was a bit of a hassle. After wearing the watch all day, I had to charge it before bed and again after waking up.

However, the Series 12 is different. Its battery is enough to last a full day plus an entire night, so now I only need to charge it after I wake up. The Apple Watch Series 12 also charges noticeably faster, which greatly reduces this annoyance. According to Apple, charging for 15 minutes provides up to 12 hours of use.

I suspect the brand-new S11 chip—based on the 2nm design from the A20 Pro—is the main reason for the significantly extended battery life. Whatever the reason, not having to worry about the sleep tracking battery issue on the Apple Watch Series 12 is fantastic. Another major advantage of the S11 chip? The Apple Watch Series 12 is noticeably faster, especially when using Siri.

Exclusive Software Features

The Series 12 finally adds an official step counter as a watch face complication, which I enjoy viewing in my Smart Stack. Will this feature roll out to older Apple Watch models? Quite possibly. After all, Apple is no stranger to counting steps. The step counting on the Apple Watch Series 12 is indeed more accurate, but given that the relevant data has long existed, I think Apple should have added this complication much sooner. Regardless, it's good that the Series 12 has this feature.

Another excellent new feature is the all-new Readiness app, which tells you how you're doing today based on your sleep the night before, the previous day's activity, and your vital signs. This is similar to WHOOP's recovery score, and I'm of course thrilled that Apple has added this feature to the Apple Watch. Unfortunately, this feature is exclusive to the Series 12, but I also understand that Apple wouldn't want to calculate this metric using less accurate data.

Summary

Overall, the Apple Watch Series 12 is a pretty impressive upgrade. This is entirely an "S" year update, but if what you care about is actual functional improvements to the Apple Watch rather than just cosmetic changes, I think this could be one of the most significant yearly upgrades since the Apple Watch Series 4.

Compared to the Series 10 and 11, the bezels are indeed slightly thicker. For users using dark watch face backgrounds, I personally can barely notice it—but I'd hope Apple improves on this further in the next generation.

Finally worth mentioning, the Apple Watch Series 12 equips the aluminum models with Ceramic Shield 2, making it more scratch-resistant than older Apple Watches. I haven't owned it long enough to truly test this, but so far, my Apple Watch still looks as good as new.
